_comment: Engines the reader matrix runs in CI. `version` is what the pins give (requirements.txt, docker-compose.yml, engines.py SPARK_IMAGE); test_harness.py checks the two agree. `job` is the job of .github/workflows/parquet-readers.yaml that runs the engine.

engines.name: pandas
engines.access: read_parquet with s3fs, filters= for pruning (2.3.x: parquet-tools pins pandas<3)

engines.name: Trino
engines.access: Hive connector, file metastore, external table

engines.name: parquet-tools
engines.access: inspect / show on one object (inspection, not a query engine)

cloud.name: Amazon Athena
cloud.note: Athena engine v3 is Trino; Hive external tables over the same S3 layout

cloud.name: Google BigQuery
cloud.note: external table over Parquet with Hive partitioning mode; no tested engine shares its reader, so nothing here proves it

cloud.name: Snowflake
cloud.note: external table with PARTITION BY over the dt/hour path; no tested engine shares its reader, so nothing here proves it

cloud.name: Databricks / Spark SQL
cloud.note: same Spark Parquet reader on s3:// or abfss://
